recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Revisit only if a final CapabilityStatement2 or successor mechanism is published that lets clients discover paging snapshot behavior; that would be a new follow-up clarification rather than a missed FHIR-39126 application.
issue_request: FHIR-39126 asked for a hard requirement that a paged search result represent the complete result set as of the initial search execution time. The final Published resolution was Not Persuasive with Modification: do not require all servers to maintain a frozen snapshot, but make the HTTP paging section explicit that behavior can vary and may later be declared through a CapabilityStatement2 mechanism.
initial_application: Commit f63bcf4e297263d89809e69f2ac86ddbeb935b0d explicitly applied FHIR-39126 by adding the Paging Continuity & Integrity subsection to source/http.html. It lists snapshot-as-was, snapshot-as-current, and repeat-search approaches and tells clients not to assume a particular paging behavior.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2022-11-14 confirm the issue was not accepted as a hard requirement and mention a future CS2 feature/flag for snapshot support. Current source/http.html remains active core RESTful API source and still contains the variable-behavior guidance. Later applied issue FHIR-51428 added nearby paging link best practices but did not alter the FHIR-39126 timing decision.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The current source already satisfies the final issue resolution and adding the originally requested hard snapshot requirement would contradict the work-group decision.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied paging best-practice guidance touched the same HTTP paging area but did not change the FHIR-39126 timing/continuity decision.
